prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — here’s a practical way to find and pick the right injury lawyer in Pleasanton (Alameda County).

1) What kind of lawyer you need
- A California personal injury attorney who handles car-accident cases (not just a general practice). Preferably one with trial experience and who handles cases on contingency (no fee unless you recover).

2) Immediate steps you should have taken / do now
- Get and keep all medical records and bills; follow medical advice.
- Get a copy of the police report.
- Preserve photos/videos of the scene, vehicle damage, your injuries, and contact info for witnesses.
- Notify your insurer (as required) but avoid recorded statements to the other side or admitting fault.
- Note: California statute of limitations for personal injury is generally 2 years from the injury. Claims against a government entity must be filed much sooner (generally within 6 months). Don’t delay contacting an attorney.

3) How to find candidates
- Use reputable sources: State Bar of California lawyer search (calbar.ca.gov), Alameda County/Contra Costa Bar Association referral services, and independent rating sites (Super Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell, Avvo). Ask friends/family for referrals.
- Search for attorneys who list “automobile accident,” “personal injury,” and “trial experience” and who have client reviews and published results.

4) What to ask in a first (usually free) consultation
- How long have you handled car-accident cases? How many cases like mine have you taken to trial?
- Do you handle cases on a contingency fee? What percentage and when is it charged? (Typical structure: ~33% if settled before suit, ~40% if after filing, higher if appeal — varies.)
- What costs will I be responsible for if we don’t win? Do you advance costs?
- Who will be my main contact (attorney or paralegal)? How often will I be updated?
- What’s your assessment of my case and likely range of value? How long might it take?
- Do you have experience with my insurer or the defendant’s employer (if relevant)?
- Can you provide references or recent case results?

5) What to bring to consultations
- Police report (or report number), photos, medical records/summary, medical bills, insurance information, date/time/location of crash, names/contacts of witnesses, and any correspondence from insurers.

6) Red flags to avoid
- Guarantees of a specific dollar amount or “I can get you millions.”
- No written fee agreement.
- Reluctance to explain fee/cost structure clearly.
- Poor responsiveness or evasive answers about experience.
- Pressure to sign immediately without reviewing the agreement.

7) Practical expectations
- Typical contingency fee ranges as above; attorney usually advances litigation costs and is repaid from recovery.
- Most cases settle without trial, but some require litigation — trial experience matters.
- Timeline: many cases settle in 6–18 months; severe/complex cases can take longer.

8) Next step I can do for you
- If you want, tell me brief facts: how severe are your injuries, whether you began treatment, who was at fault (your view), whether there was a police report, and whether the other driver has insurance. I can then:
  - Suggest what to emphasize when contacting attorneys, and
  - Draft a short message/email you can send to attorneys for an initial consult.

If you prefer, I can also draft a phone script or a sample email to reach 3–5 lawyers and compare their answers. Which would you like?
